title: PDEAgent-Bench eleven-family fixed-adapter milestone
purpose: Measure the breadth of one case-identity-independent AgentFEM scientific workflow across all eleven public PDEAgent-Bench equation families without consuming oracle-only fields or regenerating backend code for each case.
physics: Poisson, heat, linear elasticity, Helmholtz, convection--diffusion, reaction--diffusion, scalar wave, Burgers, Stokes, Navier--Stokes, and biharmonic equations

execution.command: python scripts/run_benchmark.py --agent gpt-5.1 --solver-path /path/to/agentfem/tools/pdeagent_bench_solver.py --equation-types poisson heat linear_elasticity helmholtz convection_diffusion reaction_diffusion wave burgers stokes navier_stokes biharmonic --version v2 --output /path/to/evidence
execution.evidence: Local complete-family runs of the official v2 runner at PDEAgent-Bench commit 0ba9853f82a78196796fa4eeaf0951eb4c000a00 on 21--22 August 2026. The literal gpt-5.1 agent name is only a runner-compatibility directory label: no model is called in solver-path mode. The fixed adapter was developed collaboratively with Codex (GPT-5.6-sol), while the numerical result is produced by the already-fixed AgentFEM source. Per-family final gates were Poisson 77/91, heat 40/50, linear elasticity 53/63, Helmholtz 52/62, convection--diffusion 68/84, reaction--diffusion 64/64, wave 42/42, Stokes 40/61, Burgers 41/43, Navier--Stokes 24/28, and biharmonic 57/57.

observables: All 645 public cases produced executable, schema-valid output after the periodic and constant-boundary closure repairs.
The official final gate passed 558/645 cases for an 86.5 percent micro-average.
The unweighted eleven-family macro-average was 87.3 percent, and every family exceeded 65 percent.
Burgers used one public semi-implicit transport operator and matching-face MPC constraints; Navier--Stokes used a Stokes predictor and a consistent Newton tangent.

Stokes and Navier--Stokes used public Taylor--Hood mixed fields; structured 3D Stokes used a block Q3/Q2 formulation with a constant-pressure nullspace and viscosity-scaled field preconditioner, while biharmonic cases used the recorded two-Poisson split and public-boundary auxiliary closure.
acceptance: Consume only the official public agent view and never oracle mesh, oracle finite-element order, oracle solver settings, manufactured solution, or case identity.
Require every case to execute with complete required output and retain accuracy and time failures rather than hiding them.
Require every family, the unweighted family macro-average, and the case-weighted micro-average to exceed 60 percent across all eleven families.
Keep benchmark revision, AgentFEM source identity, family denominators, closure choices, and failure taxonomy with the evidence.
limitations: This is a local fixed-adapter development result, not an official leaderboard submission and not a measurement of gpt-5.1.

Several public cases are inconsistent with their withheld references or impose unusually tight oracle-relative gates; AgentFEM follows the exposed equation and boundary contract rather than fitting case-specific reference data.
Three-dimensional mixed flow now has a reusable block formulation, but stricter MMS cases and no-exact-reference near-zero Stokes cases remain open benchmark gaps.
A fixed-adapter score demonstrates numerical and workflow coverage; it does not by itself prove an AI assistance advantage.
